note: Hand-checked background and pricing history per broker. Every entry needs a source a reader can open. 'rules' (optional) lets the build work out what the change meant in rupees: from/to use the same rule format as brokers.json, plus 'min' for a minimum brokerage in rupees. Dates are when the change took effect (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is known).

facts: 2010, as a discount broker; equity delivery has been brokerage-free since December 2015

changes.text: Zerodha stopped charging brokerage on equity delivery for individual investors. Until then it charged 0.1% or ₹20 an order, whichever was lower; companies, firms and HUFs still pay that.
Accounts that fall short of the 50% cash-margin rule started paying ₹40 instead of ₹20 per intraday F&O order.

changes.text: Groww raised its minimum brokerage per order from ₹2 to ₹5, and started passing on the depository charge on every sell (₹20 plus GST), which it had been absorbing until then.

facts: 1996 in Mumbai as Angel Broking, founded by Dinesh Thakkar; renamed Angel One in 2021
On NSE and BSE since 5 Oct 2020

changes.text: Angel One ended free equity delivery. Delivery orders now pay ₹20 or 0.1%, whichever is lower, with a ₹2 minimum.
The minimum on delivery orders went from ₹2 to ₹5, and intraday brokerage changed from ₹20 or 0.03% to ₹20 or 0.1% with a ₹5 minimum.

changes.text: Customers who joined Upstox from this date pay up to ₹20 an order on equity delivery. Customers who joined earlier kept brokerage-free delivery.
